messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: gradual rollout v4.7.0 p95 latency drift detected (+28% vs baseline) on canary slices. Autorevert scheduled in 180s. details: https://telemetry/rl/4.7.0
tia: Noted. This started right at change window start. Can we pause autorevert while we confirm scope?
omar: Oncall. If it's correlated with the new tokenizer tweak, prefer manual pin of affected slices rather than full revert. Which slices are noisy?
kelly: Looks like slices: gen-eu, gen-usw. embeddings routes fine. I can draft a short release-note update if we rollback.
rachel: If we go manual, we should pin canary back to v4.6.9 and add a brief public blurb: "small latency regression during canary rollout; rolling back one step while we investigate; no data loss." Want legal to sign off?
ops-bot: Autorevert countdown: 120s. Operator override required to suppress.
tia: I'll take operator. Suppress auto for 20m to give the team time.
tia: Running pin: `rls pin --env canary --to v4.6.9 --reason "p95 drift during change window"`
ops-bot: Operator override accepted. Autorevert suppressed for 20m. Executing pin command...
ops-bot: SUCCESS: canary pinned to v4.6.9. Traffic shifted.
omar: After pin, p95 back to baseline on gen-usw and gen-eu. Keeping pin for 30m. I'll collect traces and tag the tokenizer change as suspect.
kelly: Sending brief CS note: "We observed increased response times during a canary rollout and reverted canary to previous version while we investigate. We'll post an update within 30 minutes." Posted to #customer-notify.
rachel: Filed follow-up ticket RL-9003, assigned to infra and runtime. Include tracing links and the change window runbook.
tia: Closing loop here: manual intervention executed, autorevert suppressed, comms sent. We'll reconvene after traces. :white_check_mark:
